answers.reasoning: For a parallel z-axis the perpendicular squared offset is x_c²+y_c², not z_c². I_A,zz = 0.10 + 2(0.30²+0.40²) = 0.60 kg·m².
A uniform solid cylinder about its central longitudinal axis has I = mr²/2 = 6(0.20²)/2 = 0.12 kg·m². Length contributes to a transverse-axis formula, not this axial one.
I_C ω is angular momentum about the COM in the common body frame. Its units are kg·m²/s, not force momentum, acceleration or moment; the Euler cross term accounts for rotating-frame differentiation.
The COM acceleration magnitude is sqrt(3²+0²+4²)=5 m/s². The net external force magnitude is 4×5=20 N, not the scalar sum of components or the squared norm.
Fictitious base acceleration encodes the negative of the physical gravity vector. With physical gravity −g along upward Y0, initialize base linear acceleration +g Y0.
The terminal boundary after two links has no imposed external tip wrench when f3=n3=0. Inertial/gravitational link loads and nonzero internal joint forces or moments can still exist.
At fixed q and qddot with fixed parameters/gravity, M(q)qddot and G(q) are fixed. Velocity-dependent V(q,qdot) can change, though not every rate change must change its value.
Translational kinetic energy is 0.5×2×(3²+4²)=25 J. Rotational energy is 0.5×0.50×2²=1 J. Total is 26 J; pure z angular velocity makes the other tensor entries immaterial.
Differentiate elbow and tip positions: M11=(m1+m2)l1²+m2l2²+2m2l1l2 cos(q2); M12=M21=m2l2²+m2l1l2 cos(q2); M22=m2l2². At the stated values these are 23,15,12 kg·m².
There are C(4,2)=6 unordered distinct mixed-rate products. Four force outputs therefore require a 4×6 coefficient matrix multiplying the six-entry vector; squares belong to a separate block.
